title: The Light That Went Out
text: On a black rock in the middle of the North Sea stood a lighthouse. Its keeper was an old man named Abel, and his only company was a boy called Finn. Abel had one rule. Every night, the light must burn. No matter what. [pause] Finn once asked him why. The old man looked out at the water for a long time. Then he whispered, because the sea remembers. [pause] One November night, a storm rolled in. The waves were taller than the house. And at exactly midnight, for the first time in forty years, the light went out. [pause] Finn ran up the stairs. The lamp was cold. The glass was wet, as if something had climbed out of the sea and touched it. And Abel was gone. [pause] Far out in the dark, something answered the silence. A bell. Ringing slowly, under the water.

title: The Ship In The Fog
text: Finn searched the whole island. The kitchen. The cellar. The rocks below. All he found were Abel's boots, standing neatly at the edge of the water. [pause] Then the fog came. Thick and grey and silent. And out of the fog, a ship appeared. [pause] It was old. Older than anything Finn had seen. Its sails were torn to ribbons, and a single green lantern swung from its mast. There was no wind. And yet it was moving. [whispering] Straight toward the rock. [pause] Finn could see figures standing on the deck. Dozens of them. Not moving. Just watching. [pause] Then the green lantern turned, slowly, like an eye. And every figure on that ship lifted one hand. And pointed at him. [pause] Finn knew those faces. He had seen them in the old photographs in Abel's room. Every one of them had been lost at sea.

title: The Captain's Log
text: The ship stopped right beside the rocks. The figures were gone. Finn told himself to stay inside. Instead, his feet carried him down to the water, and onto the rotten deck. [pause] The ship smelled of salt and something older. In the captain's cabin, a book lay open on the table. The ink was still wet. [pause] The last page read, November the ninth. The light is out. We cannot find the harbour. The water is rising inside the ship, but there is no hole. Something is below us. Something big. [pause] Finn turned the page. It was blank. Then, as he watched, new words began to appear, one letter at a time. Finn. [pause] Do not. [pause] Look. [pause] Down.

Instead, his feet carried him down to the water, and onto the rotten deck. ... The ship smelled of salt and something older. In the captain's cabin, a book lay open on the table. title: Something Below
text: Of course, he looked down. [pause] Through the gaps in the floorboards, the sea glowed green. And deep in that glow, something moved. At first he thought it was a whale. Then it opened an eye. An eye as big as the ship itself. [pause] The deck groaned. Water began to pour in from nowhere, cold as ice, rising around his ankles. Then his knees. [whispering] Voices came up with it. Hundreds of them. Whispering the same words over and over. Light the lamp. Light the lamp. [pause] Finn scrambled back onto the rocks just as the ship tilted. Behind him, something enormous rose out of the water. And it was not looking at the ship. It was looking at the lighthouse. [pause] At the dark, empty lamp. [pause] And it was coming closer.

title: Light The Lamp
text: Finn ran. Up the slippery rocks. Through the door. Up the hundred and twelve stairs, with the sound of the sea climbing behind him. [pause] The whole tower shook. Windows burst. Water came pouring down the steps. Finn's hands were shaking so hard he dropped the matches twice. [pause] Outside the glass, a shape filled the sky. Dark, and wet, and ancient. Its eye pressed against the window. [whispering] Finn struck the last match. [pause] The wick caught. The great lamp roared to life. A beam of white light swept across the sea. [pause] The creature screamed. A sound so deep that Finn felt it in his bones. And then, slowly, it sank back beneath the waves. And everything went quiet. [pause] Somewhere far below, the bell rang one last time. Then it stopped.

title: The Keeper
text: At dawn, the storm was gone. The ship was gone. The sea was flat and grey, as if nothing had ever happened. [pause] Then Finn heard footsteps on the stairs. It was Abel. Soaking wet. Pale as paper. But alive. He said he did not remember anything after midnight. [pause] That evening, Finn watched the old man light the lamp, the way he had done for forty years. And for the first time, he understood the rule. The light was not there to guide the ships. It was there to keep something asleep. [pause] Abel smiled and handed him the matches. Your turn now, he said. [long pause] Finn looked down at his hands. They were still wet. And they smelled of the sea. [long pause] Far below the rock, in the deep green dark, something turned over in its sleep. And waited.
